tldr: Agent Q combines Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with a self-critique mechanism and off-policy Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to enable LLM agents to learn from both successful and unsuccessful trajectories, significantly improving multi-step reasoning in interactive web environments.
contributions: A framework combining guided MCTS search, AI self-critique feedback, and iterative off-policy DPO fine-tuning for autonomous web agents
Demonstration that learning from both successful and unsuccessful trajectories improves generalization in complex multi-step reasoning tasks
Empirical validation on WebShop benchmark and real-world booking scenarios showing substantial performance gains over baselines
Scaling search-based self-supervised data collection to realistic agent settings with offline reinforcement learning
methods: The authors introduce Agent Q, which uses Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with UCB1 heuristic to explore action trajectories over web pages, generating both successful and unsuccessful paths. A feedback language model provides AI self-critique at each node to serve as intermediate reward signals, addressing sparse environment rewards. Preference pairs are constructed by combining MCTS Q-values and AI feedback scores, then used to fine-tune the policy via an off-policy variant of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) using a replay buffer that eliminates the need for a separate reference model during training. The agent operates under a POMDP formulation with a ReAct-style architecture including planning, reasoning, environment actions, and explanation actions.
results: In the WebShop environment, Agent Q consistently outperforms behavior cloning and reinforcement fine-tuning baselines, beating average human performance when equipped with online search. On a real-world booking website using LLaMA-3 70B as the base model, zero-shot success rate improved from 18.6% to 81.7% (a 340% relative increase) after a single day of autonomous data collection, and further to 95.4% with online search capability.
limitations: Online autonomous search on the web can produce weak or unsafe agents that make risky behaviors in sensitive settings like bank transfers and information sharing
The approach requires the capability to rollback actions, which is not always possible in online realistic settings
LLM agents still struggle to generalize in interactive multi-step environments as they are not native-trained for such applications
Even strong models like GPT-4 continue to face challenges in these settings
